statement.essentials: Some people have a small separate piece of gland tissue in front of the main parotid, resting on the duct.
statement.anatomy: An accessory parotid gland, separate from the main gland, is a common variant. When present it can complicate parotidectomy and can be the site of tumours.
statement.clinical: Pooled prevalence of an accessory parotid gland was 32.1% (95% CI 21.2–44.0), higher in cadaveric studies (35.8%) than on CT (21.5%); when present it was mostly unilateral (77.8%). In 19 dissected glands it formed ESGS level V in 9 and under 5% of the gland’s weight.

numbers.label: Pooled prevalence of an accessory parotid gland
numbers.population: Cadaveric and CT studies from several regions (more from Asia than North America)

limitations: The authors note a wide discrepancy in the literature on prevalence; imaging finds fewer than dissection. The accessory lobule in the model is authored from these figures, not segmented from the scan.
disagreement: Cadaveric studies pooled to 35.8% and CT studies to 21.5%.
